issues.legal_issue: A property-transfer obligation in a compromise decree may be executed without final ascertainment of partnership accounts when that ascertainment is not a condition of the transfer.
material_facts: A compromise decree required partnership property to be transferred for a specified consideration and also referred to a sum to be finally ascertained in the partnership accounts.
The appellant argued that subsequent partnership transactions and liabilities meant the accounts had to be fully taken before the transfer could be enforced.
The Court found that the decree did not make the property transfer conditional on final ascertainment and that the amount ultimately due could not fall below the specified consideration.
issues.conclusion: The property-transfer part of the decree was executable without first finally ascertaining the partnership accounts.
issues.legal_principle: The terms of a decree are read as a whole to determine whether performance is conditional on a stated accounting. A reference to final ascertainment does not prevent execution of a specified property transfer where the decree does not make that ascertainment a condition of the transfer. No earlier cases or statutory provisions are relied on.

rule.if: compromise_decree_execution and settlement_sets_fixed_transfer_price and settlement_mentions_final_accounting and accounting_not_express_condition

predicates.compromise_decree_execution: A party sought to enforce a decree embodying a compromise.
predicates.settlement_sets_fixed_transfer_price: The compromise specified consideration for a transfer of property.
predicates.settlement_mentions_final_accounting: The compromise referred to an amount to be determined through later accounting.
predicates.accounting_not_express_condition: The compromise did not make completion of the accounting a condition of the property transfer.

issues.definition: When a party seeks execution of a compromise decree that specifies a property-transfer price and mentions later accounting without making that accounting a condition, the transfer can be enforced without final accounting.

issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary named in a compromise decree retains the right to execute it when a proposed nominee was not made an assignee and the other parties’ failure to perform prevented the nomination arrangements from being completed.
material_facts: The compromise decree gave a beneficiary the right to receive the property or nominate a purchaser.
The decree contemplated that a company would be nominated as purchaser and required the parties to arrange the company’s agreement and payment security.
The Court upheld concurrent findings that the beneficiary had taken the necessary steps to secure performance and that the other parties’ neglect prevented completion of the arrangements.
The company did not become an assignee of the decree.
issues.conclusion: The beneficiary remained entitled to execute the decree despite not completing the nomination of the company as purchaser.
issues.legal_principle: A provision naming a proposed purchaser does not, without more, assign the decree or remove the execution right given to the beneficiary. Interconnected obligations concerning nomination and the purchaser’s arrangements must be read together; a beneficiary’s execution right is not defeated where the other parties’ failure to perform prevented those arrangements. No earlier cases or statutory provisions are relied on.

rule.if: compromise_decree_execution and decree_allows_beneficiary_or_nominee_to_receive_property and nominee_arrangement_requires_other_parties_to_act and other_parties_prevented_completion and nominee_not_assigned_decree

predicates.compromise_decree_execution: A party sought to enforce a decree embodying a compromise.
predicates.decree_allows_beneficiary_or_nominee_to_: The decree provides for property to pass to a beneficiary or to a purchaser nominated by that beneficiary.
predicates.nominee_arrangement_requires_other_parti: Completion of the proposed nomination arrangement requires other parties to perform specified steps.
predicates.other_parties_prevented_completion: The other parties’ failure to perform prevented completion of the nomination arrangement despite the beneficiary taking necessary steps.
predicates.nominee_not_assigned_decree: The proposed purchaser did not receive an assignment of the decree.

issues.definition: If a compromise decree allows a beneficiary or nominee to receive property, requires other parties’ cooperation for the nomination, and those parties prevent completion without assigning the decree to the nominee, the beneficiary retains the right to execute it.
